claim: GONFH is characterized by bone damage and the collapse of femoral head structure.
source: Glucocorticoid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head (GONFH) is a common refractory joint disease characterized by bone damage and the collapse of femoral head structure.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a defining characteristic of GONFH.

claim: The exact pathological mechanisms of GONFH remain unknown.
source: However, the exact pathological mechanisms of GONFH remain unknown.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the abstract.

claim: Abnormal osteogenesis and adipogenesis associated with decreased β-catenin were observed in the necrotic femoral head of GONFH patients.
source: Here, we observed abnormal osteogenesis and adipogenesis associated with decreased β-catenin in the necrotic femoral head of GONFH patients.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Glucocorticoid exposure disrupted osteogenic/adipogenic differentiation of BMSCs by inhibiting β-catenin signaling in glucocorticoid-induced GONFH rats.
source: In vivo and in vitro studies further revealed that glucocorticoid exposure disrupted osteogenic/adipogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal cells (BMSCs) by inhibiting β-catenin signaling in glucocorticoid-induced GONFH rats.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Col2+ lineage largely contributes to BMSCs.
source: Col2+ lineage largely contributes to BMSCs and was found an osteogenic commitment in the femoral head through 9 mo of lineage trace.

claim: Col2+ lineage has an osteogenic commitment in the femoral head through 9 months of lineage trace.

claim: Specific deletion of β-catenin gene (Ctnnb1) in Col2+ cells shifted their commitment from osteoblasts to adipocytes.
source: Specific deletion of β-catenin gene (Ctnnb1) in Col2+ cells shifted their commitment from osteoblasts to adipocytes, leading to a full spectrum of disease phenotype of GONFH in adult mice.

claim: β-catenin inhibition disrupting the homeostasis of osteogenic/adipogenic differentiation contributes to the development of GONFH.

claim: GONFH disables about 100,000 Chinese annually.
